questions.question: Explain the commutative property with an example from addition and one from multiplication, and name one operation for which it fails.
questions.expected_answer: Commutative means the order can be swapped without changing the answer. 18 plus 24 equals 24 plus 18, both 42. 4 times 3 equals 3 times 4, both 12. Subtraction fails: 10 minus 4 is 6 but 4 minus 10 is not 6. Division also fails.

questions.question: Use the associative property to make 17 plus 25 plus 3 plus 5 easy, and explain your grouping.
questions.expected_answer: Group 17 with 3 to make 20 and 25 with 5 to make 30, then 20 plus 30 is 50. The property lets you choose which numbers to add first, so you choose pairs that make tens.

questions.question: Work out 5 times 23 using the distributive property and explain each step. Then explain why 348 plus 0 and 348 times 0 give different answers.
questions.expected_answer: Split 23 into 20 plus 3. Multiply each part by 5: 5 times 20 is 100 and 5 times 3 is 15. Add: 100 plus 15 is 115. Adding zero changes nothing, so 348 plus 0 is 348, but multiplying by zero means zero groups of 348, which is 0.
